newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola tightens border controls with Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Angola tightens border controls with Zaire.

text.p: Angola tightened border controls with its northern neighbour Zaire this week after an increase in people crossing into its diamond-rich Lunda Norte province, national radio said.
Quoting the Ministry of the Interior, the radio reported on Wednesday that Angolan troops had detained 24 people, some of them armed, crossing the border illegally from Zaire.
The radio said: "some of these citizens tried to enter Angolan territory illegally, forcing border troops to detain 24 of them and seize military equipment".
Angola shares long borders with Zaire where rebel soldiers led by Laurent Kabila have taken control of more than half of Zaire from President Mobutu Sese Seko's forces.
The U.N. refugee agency (UNHCR) in Angola said on Thursday it was investigating reports of Rwandan refugees crossing into Angola at the northern border town of Dundo.
"We sent a person this morning and should get a report from him very soon," UNHCR representative in Angola, Marjon Kamara, told Reuters.

Earlier this month the UNHCR headquarters in Geneva quoted unconfirmed reports of some 30,000 Rwandans, including former soldiers of the Hutu-led government, moving in the direction of the Angolan border.

Aid workers in Luanda say the Rwandan Hutus are fleeing Kabil's forces. They say the refugees are seeking refuge with Angola's former rebel UNITA movement which still controls vast areas along the Zaire border.
Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko supported UNITA during Angola's 20-year civil war which ended in 1994.
The Angolan government controls a small portion of the border around Dundo.
"If those refugees are there I can't say why they went to the government-held area and not to UNITA. It can be confusing...there are no signposts saying who controls what," Kamara said.
